title: When successful requests return bad data
scenario: This time we start from the beginning. There is no fault recorded yet. Perfect right? But Chaos Engineering as all about preparing for a disaster. And management would be furious if suddenly data is wrong and customers would stop buying. So we need to prepare for that. So please prevent/mitigate the storefront from showing wrong data.
assignment: All our technicians are busy fixing the problems from the challenges before. So you are on your own. But by now, you know the process, don't you?

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Record your baseline. Include all the data you identify as relevant from Grafana into your notes.

fields.label: Hypothesis and fault injection
fields.prompt: What could be the impact of ...?

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Introduce the fault. What happens? What is wrong? What is missing?

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Which mitigation did you choose? Why would the other mitigations not solve the problem?

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: Leave the fault on and see if your mitigation works.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: What improved? Did you successfully mitigate the problem?

solution: The main delivery company replies, but sometimes sends negative delivery days, a negative price or empty fields. Other replies are normal. Stock still works.
The requests count as successful because a reply arrived. Response checks in Grafana separately shows wrong or missing values.

Under Shipping, select Check response data and click Apply Shipping settings. Wrong replies are discarded. The last valid quote stays visible with its check time, until a new valid quote updates it. If there is no earlier valid quote, delivery information is unavailable. Stock still works.

Responses rejected in Grafana counts the discarded replies even while the last valid quote remains visible. The checker does not fix the delivery company or call the backup. Remove the response fault and restore defaults to finish.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.explanation: What fault should you introduce? The data reaches the storefront but is it correct?.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.explanation: A successful request only means that a reply arrived. It can still contain wrong values. Look at Response checks in Grafana.

hints.title: Hint 3
hints.explanation: A timeout stops waiting. A breaker pauses failed requests. Neither checks the values in a reply. So maybe we should check if the data is correct.
